Residents of La Azteca, described as Laredo's oldest neighborhood, are asking for protections and more information about a proposed federal border wall — and for independent studies of flooding and environmental impacts before any construction moves forward, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

On October 17, during the annual Día del Río gathering at Las Palmas, residents and supporters presented a petition with 240 signatures to U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar. District III Councilmember Melissa Cigarroa attended the presentation and said Cuellar pledged to keep seeking protections for Las Palmas and had supported legislative language to exclude sensitive areas, the paper reports.

The concerns are close to home: residents fear harm to their homes, to neighborhood green space, to access to the Rio Grande, and to the environment — along with flooding risk and possible displacement. The Rio Grande International Study Center and the No Border Wall Coalition are among the groups involved, and speakers at a recent City Council meeting urged protection of the multigenerational neighborhood and Las Palmas, including the Las Palmas Trail at Justo Penn Park.

The wall remains a federal project, and no city action approving or blocking construction in La Azteca had been taken, according to the article — which is exactly why residents are pressing for answers and independent studies now, before construction decisions are locked in.

What to watch next: whether federal officials provide the flooding and environmental studies residents are requesting, and whether the protections Cuellar pledged for Las Palmas take shape in legislation or agency action.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “Residents of Laredo's oldest neighborhood seek border wall protections,” October 25, 2026.

title: La Azteca residents press for border wall protections with 240-signature petition to Cuellar
